paper.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: Reflexion reinforces frozen language agents through linguistic feedback: the agent reflects on task feedback and stores reflections in an episodic memory buffer read in subsequent trials, improving decision-making, reasoning and coding over baselines.

evidence.quote: converts binary or scalar feedback from the environment into verbal feedback in the form of a textual summary
evidence.support_explanation: Core operation: sparse feedback amplified into verbal text.

evidence.quote: the evaluation signal is amplified to natural language experience summaries
evidence.support_explanation: The manufactured signal is the load-bearing step.

evidence.quote: maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer to induce better decision-making in subsequent trials
evidence.support_explanation: Persisted non-weight state read in later trials.

evidence.quote: we bound mem by a maximum number of stored experiences
evidence.support_explanation: Bounded sliding window (Ω usually 1–3); no gate/curation.

evidence.quote: we truncate the agent’s memory to the last 3 self-reflections
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld memory = last 3 reflections.

evidence.quote: In the baseline runs, if self-reflection is suggested, we skip the self-reflection process, reset the environment, and start a new trial.
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld baseline gets the same retries without memory: store-off control.

evidence.quote: ReAct + Reflexion significantly outperforms ReAct by completing 130 out of 134 tasks
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld headline with denominator.

evidence.quote: In the ReAct-only approach, we see that performance increase halts between trials 6 and 7.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline plateau under equal retries.

evidence.quote: we use exact match answer grading using the environment to give a binary success signal to the agent
evidence.support_explanation: HotPotQA retry signal is ground-truth EM on the scored item (privileged signal).

evidence.quote: ReAct-only, CoT-only, and CoT (GT)-only implementations fail to probabilistically improve on any tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines reportedly never fix a failed question on retry (T=0.7); unverified, no pass@k control.

evidence.quote: In the Reflexion runs, we allowed the agent to gather experience and retry on failed tasks until it produced 3 consecutive failed attempts
evidence.support_explanation: Reflexion retry budget; baseline budget not stated.

evidence.quote: self-reflection improves learning by an 8% absolute boost over the episodic memory learning advantage
evidence.support_explanation: Reflection vs raw-trajectory memory ablation (CoT-GT, 100 questions).

evidence.quote: Reflexion improves search, information retrieval, and reasoning capabilities on 100 HotPotQA questions
evidence.support_explanation: HotPotQA n=100.

evidence.quote: The base strategy is a single code generation sample.
evidence.support_explanation: Code baseline is one sample; compute not matched.

evidence.quote: the false positive test execution rate for MBPP Python is 16.3% while the rate for HumanEval Python is a mere 1.4%

Searched §3–4 and App. A–D: memory is per instance and reset; no experiment carries reflections to other questions/environments.

signatures.object: Per-instance episodic memory of self-written reflections in the actor prompt (policy = {LLM, mem}).
signatures.information: Actor sees last 1–3 reflections and current trajectory; reflector sees trajectory + feedback; evaluator = EM oracle (HotPotQA), env success + heuristic/LLM (ALFWorld), self-generated unit tests (code).
signatures.operation: Trial → evaluate → reflect → append to memory → retry until pass/limit.
signatures.output: Final trial output; reflections are instance-specific.
signatures.feedback: Binary/scalar reward amplified to text; ≤6 AST-filtered self-tests for code.
signatures.selection_rule: None for memory content (append, sliding window); early stop when self-tests pass.
signatures.persistence: Within instance only; reset between instances.
signatures.later_use: Next trial of the same instance.
signatures.failure_boundary: MBPP-Py false positives, weak models, WebShop, local minima.

gap.author_gap: Learning from trial and error with RL needs many samples and fine-tuning; self-refinement methods lack persistent memory and work on single generations.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and tabulated; the 'no weight updates' framing is background.
lineage: Self-Refine, Pryzant et al., beam search, retry patterns
gap.closest_adjacent: Self-Refine (no memory) and Self-Debugging (execution feedback, no reflection memory).
gap.residue: Lasting, transferable improvement beyond retrying the same instance is not addressed.
gap.stakes: Cheap interpretable learning for black-box agents.
gap.method_response: Verbal reflection carried as memory into the next trial.
gap.remaining_gap: Cross-task transfer, memory curation, evaluator reliability, exploration-heavy tasks.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Gains are across trials of the instances that provide the feedback; memory is per instance and reset, so no retained-for-later-tasks evidence.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With a usable per-instance feedback signal and a strong LLM, stored self-reflections raise success over repeated trials relative to memoryless retries and raw-trajectory memory, with honest negatives.

G.reason: Concrete gap (credit assignment from sparse reward; no cross-trial memory in Self-Refine/beam search/CodeT/Self-Debugging), tabulated against neighbours; 'no weight updates' is background. Contemporary memory agents not contrasted.

M.reason: Three-role mechanism explains how a scalar becomes actionable text, with a testable ordering (reflection > raw memory > none) and acknowledged evaluator dependence.

X.reason: Loop, evaluators, window sizes, test generation and filter are reproducible; failure regimes and information permissions (EM oracle) are stated. No gate, curation, versioning or cross-task store — consistent with its within-instance claim, so not 4.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmarks with environment success / exact match / hidden benchmark tests for the final code score, plus a measured reliability analysis of the self-test verifier (FP/FN). Oracle use, unmatched compute and small n are judged under holdout, causality and statistics respectively.

E.causality.reason: Store-off arms exist in each domain: memoryless retries with equal resets (ALFWorld), raw-trajectory memory vs reflection (HotPotQA), reflection omission with tests and retries kept (Rust-50). Missing: pass@k-matched control for the HumanEval headline, verified HotPotQA retry baseline.

E.holdout.reason: Code: loop sees only self-generated tests, final score uses hidden tests, and a post-cutoff set controls contamination. HotPotQA/ALFWorld: the scored item's success signal drives retries (EM oracle). No cross-instance holdout for memory.

E.statistics.reason: Denominators and honest negatives are reported (MBPP regression, StarChat, WebShop), but headline results are single runs without any uncertainty; ablation n=50 (0.60→0.68 = four problems).

E.cost.reason: Trial limits and memory windows given, but no call/token/cost accounting; code baseline is single-sample.

reason: Complete pinned text read; non-weight memory retained across trials and read by the frozen actor (boundary A-class, within-instance only); scored on its scoped claim.

resolutions.reason: Primary must be the load-bearing operation: the authors define the contribution as amplifying sparse feedback into a verbal signal (D01, D02); conditioning is the delivery channel and stays as supporting.
Both operations are distinct and both executed; two matches, sub-cards null.
sol's composite expectation mixed retention, memory ablation and new-task transfer; splitting shows transfer is unmet while store-off is partial.
Causality part matches son55 RE-baseline (partial); cost part is unmet (no accounting).
Both seats: grounding signals explicit and self-test error/negatives reported.
Lessons always formed on the scored instance; GT EM on HotPotQA.
Store-off arms exist; budgets partly unmatched.

son55's reasons for 2 (EM oracle drives retries, small n, multi-trial vs single sample) are holdout, statistics and causality issues already scored there; counting them here double-penalises. On measurement proper: standard success/EM/hidden-test metrics plus a measured FP/FN analysis of the self-test verifier → 3.

sol's alternative ('extra generations/feedback budget') is controlled where it matters: ALFWorld baseline gets equal resets (D06, D08) and the Rust reflection-omission arm keeps tests and retries (D17). Store-off evidence in all three domains; remaining gaps (HumanEval pass@k, HotPotQA retry baseline) keep it below 4.

Code results are decoupled (self-tests in loop, hidden tests for scoring) with a post-cutoff contamination control; HotPotQA/ALFWorld use the scored item's success signal; no cross-instance holdout. Mixed → 2 (sol's 1 ignored the code decoupling).

Denominators and negatives are reported but headline results have no uncertainty at all (single runs, n=100/50/40). Calibrated against this batch: Gödel Agent (bootstrap CIs + 100-trial failure denominator) = 2, GrIPS (seeds + CIs + tests) = 3; Reflexion sits below both → 1.
